text:
cara (CSE): FYI customer reported a sharp increase in hallucinations after today's canary. they say model is inventing citations and wrong dates. :frowning_face:

sachin: which customer and which model? any repro payload?

cara (CSE): acme corp on hosted API, model 'redwood-open-8k-v2', happened ~11:10am UTC after canary. sending a sanitized example.

cara (CSE): ```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n -H 'Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY' \n -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n -d '{"model":"redwood-open-8k-v2","input":"Summarize the following meeting notes and list any stated deadlines.","max_tokens":200,"temperature":0.0}'
```

cara (CSE): customer got: ```
"summary": "Project kickoff on March 15, 2026. Deliverable due April 1, 2026. See appendix: internal roadmap v2."
"sources": ["acme-internal:roadmap-v2.pdf"]
```

cara (CSE): all of that is false for their notes. they never mentioned dates or that doc.

elena: ugh. any errors/latency spikes in the same window? might be a routing to a different model variant or a decoding change.

repro-bot: quick check against prod-stable (pinned) vs canary-run:
- prod-stable -> no hallucination in 20/20 runs
- canary-run -> hallucination in 7/20 runs
(details: sampling seeds randomized)

sachin: can we see the rollout that hit hosted? which flag changed? @deploy-bot can you paste the canary diff?

deploy-bot: Rollout 2026-03-17T11:05Z applied: 
- enabled speculative decoding (draft-prefetch) default=true for redwood-open-8k-v2-canary
- sampling backend: new speculative policy v3
(rollout id: rlt-20260317-11-05)

elena: speculative decoding would alter how drafts are validated and merged — can increase coherence for many prompts but I've seen it hallucinate with temp=0.0 on instruction prompts when merge heuristics are aggressive.

tom (oncall): i've paused the canary routing for that pool (rlt-20260317-11-05) — traffic reverted to prod-stable.

cara (CSE): customer is waiting, can you confirm rollback and ETA for fix?

deploy-bot: Rollback executed: rlt-20260317-11-05 -> state: paused at 2026-03-17T11:22Z by tom (oncall).

repro-bot: running an A/B repro now with the exact sanitized prompt and headers the customer used (sampling: temp=0.0, top_p=1). i'll post counts.

repro-bot: results: prod-stable 0/50 hallucinate, canary (speculative enabled) 18/50 hallucinate.

sachin: that's a big delta. elena, can you bisect the speculative changes? maybe the merge heuristic or the scoring threshold was decreased.

elena: will start a narrow bisect on the speculative code path. initial guess: draft-merge alpha threshold lowered from 0.8 -> 0.6 in policy v3.

cara (CSE): customer confirmed they see improvement after we paused. they asked for an incident summary and rollback note.

tom (oncall): logging request/response pairs for the affected window saved to /var/logs/canary-hits/1948723456.zip (access: eng-sre).

cara (CSE): thanks — i'll send the customer a note: we paused the canary, investigating decoding merge behavior, will follow up with a root cause and mitigation. :thumbsup:

sachin: follow-up action items: (1) elena to revert or tighten merge threshold for speculative path; (2) run large scale eval on customer-like instruction prompts; (3) add telemetry to detect hallucination upticks post-deploy and auto-pause.

elena: ack, starting on (1) now. i'll share a small PR and measurement dashboard when ready.

cara (CSE): please cc me on the PR so i can loop acme back in.

repro-bot: scheduled a longer run overnight (10k queries) comparing prod-stable vs speculative-v3. will report in morning.

cara (CSE): customer also flagged billing: they were charged normal usage; no billing break. just quality.

tom (oncall): note for postmortem: include canary vetting checklist and add a prompt-suite for enterprise customers covering hallucination detection.

sachin: thanks everyone. good quick catch and revert. we'll keep thread open until elena posts PR and repro-bot posts the overnight run.

cara (CSE): closing loop with customer now, will update here when they confirm final state.
